cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: In-house manufacturing with no outsourcing of production. All key manufacturing processes for engineered garment manufacturing are available in-house, including seam sealing, bonded and stitch-free assembly, laser cutting, ultrasonic welding, reflective fusing, quilting and down filling; the DRHP states that keeping these processes under one roof allows better control of quality, production time and cost. The manufacturing process runs Material Inward, Fabric and Accessory Checking, Fabric Cutting, Sewing and Technical Assembly, Ironing, Checking/Finishing and Final Packing, with quality-control checkpoints at each stage. Upstream, the Company is not backward integrated into fabric: raw materials are primarily sourced from third-party suppliers in international and local markets - fabric development is carried out through external suppliers, and waterproof membranes, seam-sealing tapes, coatings, reflective materials, waterproof zippers and yarns are sourced from suppliers in Europe, the Far East and other markets. Imported purchases were 73.80% of total purchases for the period ended September 30, 2025, 71.47% in Fiscal 2025, 63.89% in Fiscal 2024 and 69.38% in Fiscal 2023 (Rs.1,123.45 / 2,581.21 / 1,130.33 / 1,220.18 lakhs), with domestic purchases at 26.20%, 28.53%, 36.11% and 30.62% (Rs.398.74 / 1,030.25 / 638.81 / 538.61 lakhs) respectively. Inbound materials move by sea for planned orders with longer lead times and by air for sampling and urgent programmes; outbound finished garments are exported by sea for regular production shipments and by air for express and seasonal deliveries, with stated proximity to Tuticorin port and Chennai sea port and airport. Power is met through the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited and solar power panels installed at the factory; water is met through the Tiruppur City Municipal Corporation. The Company states it has no collaborations, tie-ups or joint ventures and no export obligation as on the date of the DRHP.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Woven garments contributed 61.70% of revenue from product sales for the six-month period ended September 30, 2025 (Rs. 2,366.45 lakhs) and 72.39% in Fiscal 2025 (Rs. 3,823.39 lakhs); any decline from competition, pricing pressure or demand/supply fluctuation would adversely affect results
- The top customer contributed 41.02% of sales as of September 30, 2025 and approximately 51.51%, 38.13% and 42.01% in Fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023; top 10 customers accounted for 100%, 99.70%, 99.21% and 99.13% of sales in the same periods, and customers often undertake vendor rationalisation
- Switzerland accounted for 74.88% of revenue for the period 01/04/2025 to 30/09/2025 and 58.87% in FY2024-25, with supply largely to various departments of the Government of Switzerland
- Exports accounted for 99.83% of revenue from operations for the period ended September 30, 2025, 93.87% in FY2025, 87.77% in FY2024 and 94.99% in FY2023, concentrating exposure to European and North American demand and cross-border trade conditions
- All manufacturing operations are presently carried out at one facility in Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu, with an installed capacity of 450,000 garment pieces per annum
- Existing production capacity is stated to be operating at near-optimal utilisation levels; incremental growth depends on commissioning the proposed additional facility of approximately 1.41 acres at Tiruppur
- Net worth was negative at Rs. (231.53) lakhs in FY2022-23, and RoE for that year was disclosed as not meaningful because average shareholders' equity was negative; net worth has since risen to Rs. 1,382.25 lakhs (FY2024-25) and Rs. 1,931.26 lakhs as of September 30, 2025
- Raw material sourcing and fabric development are carried out through external suppliers, with global suppliers relied on for seam-sealing tapes, reflective materials, waterproof zippers and specialized coatings

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up a new manufacturing facility at Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu, spread over approximately 1.41 acres and dedicated to complex outerwear and high-performance products, funded from Fresh Issue Net Proceeds.**
- **The proposed additional manufacturing facility is to be established over approximately 1.41 acres in Tiruppur to increase production capacity, enhance technical capabilities and improve operational efficiencies.**
- **The amount of Net Proceeds utilised for General Corporate Purposes shall not exceed 15% of the Gross Proceeds or Rs. 10 crores, whichever is lower.**
- **The Issue comprises a Fresh Issue of up to 35,52,000 Equity Shares of face value of Rs. 10 each, proposed to be listed on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE).**
- **Continue making investments in technological capabilities to raise product standards and meet diverse client requirements, given that existing production capacity is operating at near-optimal utilisation.**
- **Build relationships with premium outdoor and performance wear brands in Europe and North America by approaching select brands, offering production capacity, showcasing the facility and certifications and providing samples of seam-sealed, …**
- **Continue investing in quality control infrastructure, including testing equipment and trained personnel, to maintain consistency of output as production volumes increase with the planned capacity expansion.**
- **Maintain procurement relationships with global suppliers of technical materials and invest in training and development of the workforce, particularly on seam-sealing machines, ultrasonic welders and laser cutters.**
- **Continue benchmarking costs at each cost center against industry/scientific standards to control direct costs and overheads, maintaining cost discipline while increasing output at the new facility.**
- **The existing Tiruppur facility carries an installed capacity of 450,000 garment pieces per annum across a built-up area of over 45,000 square feet.**
- **Management flags dependence on woven garments, which contributed 61.70% of revenue from product sales for the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 72.39% in Fiscal 2025, with no assurance that this sales level can be maintained.**
